feedback.evidence: Authenticated browser DOM showed 2026-08-17 08:50:52; application-local.yml declares serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai but V43 and many platform migrations rely on database CURRENT_TIMESTAMP while APIs expose LocalDateTime without an offset.

feedback.causal_hypothesis: The JDBC connection timezone parses values as Shanghai but does not force the MySQL session timezone, so CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is evaluated in the UTC container session and loses zone context in DATETIME/LocalDateTime.

data.decision_reason: The observed eight-hour display offset is real and non-critical, but its cause is the platform-wide database-session, storage, and timezone-less API contract. A release-only correction would create inconsistent timestamp semantics across modules.

causal_assessment.hypothesis: MySQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is evaluated in the UTC container session while JDBC and JSON expose timezone-less LocalDateTime values interpreted as Shanghai wall time.
supporting_evidence: The binding operation performed around 16:50 displayed as 08:50:52.
application-local.yml declares serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai, but there is no central forceConnectionTimeZoneToSession or offset-bearing API contract.
Multiple existing platform migrations and services use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and LocalDateTime, so the causal surface is not release-specific.
causal_assessment.falsifier: A controlled connection showing MySQL session time_zone already set to Asia/Shanghai while the same stored instant and API serialization still reproduce the offset.
